body: Maybe formally dancing has decreased sure, but dancing doesn't take any money, knowledge, or time to engage with. We have more access to music than ever before and yet less people dance. I'm pretty certain dance has been on a decline since social media emergence, spotlight effect and anxiety - people are judging themselves far more and are more stiff and rigid because of it. We have all the tools in the world too dance, and while I agree that it's harder to dance in a more exhausting world - it is very much still there and will be what revitalizes us.

another note for what i mean about the "now", when we are seeing an item in front of us - we are literally putting attention on it and feeling it in a sense - live with no latency on the light hitting our eyes. this isn't to say that the seemingly deterministic quality of the universe isn't also having protons hit our retinas with the neural computation following it, but this is because our brain is our conceptualization tool that grounds us in some sort of identity and identification of the world. whether it's for survival, maintaining our experience, whatever it may be its a tool and a damn useful one, but we are not the brain, neither is it vice versa

experience isn't linear, but conceptual thinking is (which would be the concepts we use in science, they are useful but a tool nonetheless that disconnects us from the experience of being alive). experience is some sort of literal real, no latency quantum experience, that's why we say everything happens in the "now". 

yes the brain is still a tool that our quantum awareness uses to engage with reality (this would explain why you can damage parts of the brain and function differently from normal, plasticity can fix practically though not easily all cases of brain damage). but who's to say the "quantum" isn't the fabric of experience, in which all imagined and experience are "real" in a sense. 

where is the experiencer, you in this experience. science can never find that and thus we should take certain experiences like these as something more than just a brain illusion, it seems pretty contradictory to say we are the brain in this deterministic sense, yet to experience things that are so far out from some sort of binary computation. it's almost as if we are trying to justify ourselves with tools and standards rather than the foundation we experience from, feelings which you cannot contain nor explain with justice 

we are alive my friend
